data.title: Anthropic Is Set to Debut on Nasdaq Today. Defiance's 2X Daily ETFs, ANTC and ANTQ, Are Expected Monday
data.description:
Anthropic's Nasdaq Debut

Anthropic's debut comes ahead of the expected launch of two Defiance ETFs tied to its share price. The Defiance 2X ANT Long Daily ETF (Nasdaq: ANTC) and the Defiance 2X ANT Short Daily ETF (Nasdaq: ANTQ) are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq at 9:30 a.m. ET on Monday, November 23. Both are single-stock ETFs with one-day objectives: ANTC seeks 200% of the daily percentage change in ANT's share price and ANTQ seeks -200%, before fees and expenses.

Anthropic made its registration statement public on October 26, set a price range of $70 to $78 a share on November 10 and kept those terms in its amended filing of November 17. The offering priced on Wednesday, November 18, at $83 a share.

The deal covers 980 million shares of Class A common stock: about 956.4 million sold by Anthropic and about 23.6 million sold by existing stockholders. The underwriters hold an option on up to 147 million more shares from the company. At the IPO price the 980 million shares are worth about $81.3 billion. Goldman Sachs (NYSE: GS) and Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) are the first of 22 underwriters named on the prospectus cover.

Seven companies have also agreed to buy $26.0 billion of non-voting Class N common stock at the IPO price in a private placement alongside the offering: Advanced Micro Devices (Nasdaq: AMD), Broadcom (Nasdaq: AVGO), Alphabet's Google (Nasdaq: GOOGL), Micron Technology (Nasdaq: MU), Microsoft (Nasdaq: MSFT), NVIDIA (Nasdaq: NVDA) and TSMC Partners, a subsidiary of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM).

Nasdaq has approved the Class A shares for listing, and trading is expected to open today. The opening price will be set in Nasdaq's opening auction and can differ from the IPO price.

The Company Behind the Ticker

Anthropic is the AI research lab behind Claude, which it delivers through its models, its developer platform and applications such as Claude Code. It was founded in 2021, is based in San Francisco and is organized as a Delaware public benefit corporation.

Revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $33.2 billion, compared with $2.5 billion a year earlier, according to the prospectus. The third quarter alone brought in $17.0 billion. More than 11,900 customers each accounted for at least $100,000 of revenue over the prior twelve months.

The losses are also large. Anthropic reported a $1.3 billion loss from operations for the nine months and a net loss of $104.0 billion, of which $94.3 billion came from changes in the fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs. It has committed to about $900.9 billion of future spending, nearly all of it on computing capacity and infrastructure, and expects to incur about $451.6 billion of that before the end of 2030. It held $95.6 billion of cash and cash equivalents at September 30.

Voting control rests with the co-founders and a trust. Class A shares carry one vote each. A single Class F share, held by an entity of the co-founders, carries 50.1% of the voting power on general matters, and the Long-Term Benefit Trust elects a majority of the board. Nasdaq rules classify Anthropic as a controlled company.

Information about Anthropic and the other companies named is drawn from Anthropic's SEC filings and is included for illustrative purposes only. It is not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Anthropic is not affiliated with Defiance ETFs, Tidal Trust II or the funds.

What ANTC and ANTQ Are Designed to Do

Defiance ETFs, a Miami-based issuer of thematic, leveraged and income ETFs, built the pair for traders who want a one-day position on ANT's share price, long or short, through a single ticker.

Each fund targets the percentage change in ANT's share price over a single day, measured from one close of regular trading to the next. ANTC seeks daily investment results, before fees and expenses, of two times (200%) that change. ANTQ seeks -2 times (-200%). On a day when ANT rises 3%, ANTC is designed to gain about 6% and ANTQ to lose about 6%, before fees, expenses and financing costs. On a day when ANT falls 3%, the results reverse.

Neither fund seeks its objective over any period longer than one trading day.

The funds do not own Anthropic stock. They get their exposure through swap agreements with financial institutions and may also use listed options, and they hold collateral such as U.S. government securities and money market funds. At or near each close, the adviser rebalances each fund so the next session starts with exposure of about 200% or -200%. Shareholders of ANTC and ANTQ have no voting rights in Anthropic and no right to any dividends it pays.

Both funds are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq at 9:30 a.m. ET on Monday, November 23. Shares cannot be purchased until the funds begin trading, and the expected date may change. Once listed, each will trade like any other ETF, through a standard brokerage account.

How the Daily Reset Works

Because exposure resets every day, a fund's return over a week or a month is the compounded result of its daily returns. That result will very likely differ from 200% or -200% of ANT's return over the same period, and the difference tends to widen as volatility rises.

According to the prospectus, each fund will lose money if ANT's performance is flat over time. Each can also lose money over a period longer than a day in which ANT moves in its favor: ANTC while ANT rises, ANTQ while ANT falls.

Both funds are designed as short-term trading vehicles for knowledgeable investors who monitor their positions frequently. They are not suitable for all investors.

Inside the Funds

ANTC and ANTQ are series of Tidal Trust II and are expected to list on The Nasdaq Stock Market. Tidal Investments LLC is the investment adviser and Defiance ETFs, LLC is the fund sponsor.

Each fund charges a 0.69% management fee and estimates 0.02% of other expenses, for total annual fund operating expenses of 0.71%. That total leaves out the financing costs embedded in the funds' swap agreements, which the prospectus treats as an indirect expense.

Fund Snapshot

Fund details are from the prospectus dated November 6, 2026. The launch date is expected and subject to change.

The Bottom Line

Anthropic's shares are expected to start trading today. ANTC and ANTQ are expected to follow at 9:30 a.m. ET on Monday, November 23. One seeks 200% of the daily percentage change in ANT's share price and the other seeks -200%, before fees and expenses, and each lists total annual fund operating expenses of 0.71%. Both funds work one trading day at a time. Over longer periods their returns will very likely differ from those multiples, and either fund can lose money quickly.

Learn More About ANTC and ANTQ

The prospectus and fund details are available at defianceetfs.com/anthropic-etfs or by calling 833.333.9383.

Risks Investors Should Weigh

The objective lasts one trading day. Each fund seeks its stated multiple for a single day, measured close to close. Over longer periods, compounding means returns will very likely differ from 200% or -200% of ANT's return, and the difference widens with volatility.

A flat stock still costs money. The prospectus states that each fund will lose money if ANT's performance is flat over time. ANTC can lose money over a period longer than a day even if ANT rises, and ANTQ can lose money over such a period even if ANT falls.

One day can take the whole investment. If ANT's share price falls by more than 50% in a single trading day, ANTC investors could lose all of their money. If it rises by more than 50% in a single trading day, ANTQ investors would lose all of their money.

One company, new to public trading. Both funds depend entirely on a stock that is expected to begin trading today and has no public trading history. Newly listed shares can be highly volatile, and a halt in trading of ANT is expected to halt trading in the funds as well.

Exposure comes through derivatives. The funds use swaps and may use listed options in place of owning ANT, which adds counterparty risk. The prospectus also warns that swap and options capacity in a recently listed stock may be limited. A fund that cannot get enough exposure may miss its daily objective and may trade at wider spreads or away from net asset value.

Anthropic's risks carry through. ANT is assigned to the software industry, so both funds are concentrated there. Anthropic's own prospectus lists risks that include securing enough computing capacity, intense competition, an evolving and uncertain regulatory environment, litigation tied to its AI models, reliance on a limited number of customers and cloud providers, and a capital structure that limits the influence of Class A stockholders.

New funds. ANTC and ANTQ have no operating history. Their shares may trade above or below net asset value, and bid-ask spreads may be wider in early sessions.

Disclosures

This article is sponsored content created in partnership with Defiance ETFs. It is intended for informational and educational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice, a recommendation, or an offer or solicitation to buy or sell any security.

IMPORTANT DISCLOSURES

Defiance ETFs, LLC is the fund sponsor. Tidal Investments LLC is the investment adviser.

The Funds' investment objectives, risks, charges, and expenses must be considered carefully before investing. The prospectus and summary prospectus contain this and other important information about the investment company. Please read the prospectus and/or summary prospectus carefully before investing. For a prospectus or summary prospectus, go to defianceetfs.com/anthropic-etfs. Hard copies can be requested by calling 833.333.9383.

Investing involves risk. Principal loss is possible. The Funds seek daily leveraged (ANTC) or daily inverse leveraged (ANTQ) investment results and are intended to be used as short-term trading vehicles. They are riskier than alternatives that do not use leverage or short strategies and are not suitable for all investors. The Funds are intended only for knowledgeable investors who understand the consequences of seeking daily leveraged or daily inverse leveraged results and who will monitor their positions frequently. An investor could lose the full principal value of an investment within a single day.

As ETFs, the Funds may trade at a premium or discount to NAV. Shares are bought and sold at market price (not NAV) and are not individually redeemed from the Funds. ANTC and ANTQ are expected to begin trading on November 23, 2026. Shares cannot be purchased until the Funds begin trading, and the expected date may change.

ANT Risks. Each Fund's exposure to Anthropic (ANT) comes through swap agreements and options based on ANT's share price. Investors in the Funds have no voting rights in ANT and no right to receive dividends or other distributions from ANT. ANT has little or no public trading history, and its share price may be highly volatile. ANT's business depends on its AI models and platform, and its structure as a public benefit corporation with concentrated voting control differs from that of most public companies. ANTQ will lose money when ANT's share price rises.

Compounding and Market Volatility Risk. Each Fund has a single-day investment objective. Its performance for periods longer than one trading day will be the result of each day's returns compounded over the period, which will very likely differ from 200% (ANTC) or -200% (ANTQ) of ANT's performance for that period, before fees and expenses. Higher volatility increases this effect.

Leverage Risk. ANTC obtains leveraged exposure through derivatives, which magnifies losses. If ANT's share price decreases by more than 50% on a given trading day, ANTC's investors could lose all of their money.

Short Sale Exposure Risk. ANTQ obtains inverse leveraged exposure through derivatives. ANTQ could lose an amount greater than its net assets if ANT's share price increases by more than 50% on a given trading day, and its investors would lose all of their money.

Derivatives and Counterparty Risk. The Funds use swap agreements and may use listed options. Derivatives may be more volatile than, and may not correlate perfectly with, the underlying security. Swap agreements expose the Funds to the risk that a counterparty will not meet its obligations.

Recent IPO and Derivatives Capacity Constraints Risk. Because ANT has little or no public trading history, the swap and options capacity available to the Funds may be limited. If a Fund cannot obtain sufficient exposure, it may not achieve its investment objective and its shares may trade at wider bid-ask spreads or at premiums or discounts to NAV.

Intra-Day Investment Risk. The Funds seek their objectives from the close of regular trading on one trading day to the close on the next. An investor who buys shares at any other time will likely have more or less than 200% or -200% exposure to ANT for the rest of that day.

Single Issuer and Software Industry Concentration Risk. Each Fund's performance depends on one company. Each Fund is also concentrated in the software industry, the industry to which ANT is assigned, and may be more volatile than a fund invested across industries.

Trading Halt Risk. Trading in ANT or in the Funds' shares may be halted. A halt may prevent a Fund from achieving its objective and may prevent investors from buying or selling shares.

Non-Diversification Risk. Each Fund is non-diversified and may be more sensitive to a single economic, business, or regulatory event than a diversified fund.

New Fund Risk. The Funds are recently organized investment companies with no operating history, so prospective investors have no track record on which to base their investment decisions.

Information about Anthropic in this article is drawn from the company's SEC filings and other publicly available sources. Defiance ETFs has not independently verified this information. None of the Funds, Tidal Trust II, or Tidal Investments LLC is affiliated, connected, or associated with Anthropic, and the Funds are not sponsored, endorsed, or approved by the company. References to other companies are for illustrative purposes only and are not a recommendation to buy or sell any security.

Brokerage commissions may be charged on trades.

What travels with the article but is not part of it: the fields to complete once Anthropic prices, the checks for Thursday morning, the ticker tags, the SEO keywords and the sources.

Fill-Ins on Pricing Night

Two fields, each used twice (Story Highlights and Anthropic's Nasdaq Debut). All four spots are in bold brackets.

  • IPO price: the per-share price Anthropic announces Wednesday evening.
  • Gross proceeds: 825,000,000 shares times the IPO price. That is $57.75 billion at $70, $61.05 billion at $74 and $64.35 billion at $78. Each $1 on the price moves the total by $825 million, so $80 comes to $66.0 billion and $85 to about $70.1 billion.

The header image slot under the date line takes the paired ANTC and ANTQ card.

Re-Check Thursday Morning Before It Publishes

  • Deal size: if the offering is upsized, four numbers change: 825 million shares, about 801.4 million from Anthropic, about 23.6 million from selling stockholders and the option on 123.75 million more. The gross proceeds math changes with them.
  • Price range sentence: the article says Anthropic set a $70 to $78 range on November 10 and kept it in the November 17 filing. Update that sentence if a new range is filed before pricing.
  • Before or after ANT opens: the article is written to run before ANT's first trade. If it publishes after the open, five spots move from "expected" to past tense: the headline, the first sentence of Story Highlights, the last paragraph of Anthropic's Nasdaq Debut, the first sentence of The Bottom Line and the "One company, new to public trading" risk.

  • Monday at 9:30 a.m. ET: stated in Story Highlights, Anthropic's Nasdaq Debut, What ANTC and ANTQ Are Designed to Do and The Bottom Line, always as expected. The Fund Snapshot and the disclosures give the date only.
  • Links: every fund link points to defianceetfs.com/anthropic-etfs. Swap in the ANTC and ANTQ fund pages if they are live.

What Differs From the Earlier Friday-Launch Draft

  • The launch is Monday, November 23 at 9:30 a.m. ET, not Friday, November 20, and the article no longer describes the launch as coming the day after the IPO.
  • The article runs before ANT's first trade, so the debut is "expected" throughout and the disclosures use the wording that holds before ANT lists.
  • The IPO sections now come ahead of the fund sections.
  • ANTQ's single-day loss sentence matches the prospectus cover: investors "would" lose all of their money if ANT rises more than 50% in a day. ANTC's stays "could."
  • The flat-performance sentence covers both funds, as the prospectus does.
  • Offering details were checked again against Anthropic's November 17 amendment. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are described as the first underwriters named on the cover, because the filing does not label them as leads.

data.title: Dell and HPE Stocks Rise After Lenovo's Q2 Earnings — Here's Why
data.description:
Shares of PC maker Dell Technologies (DELL) and server manufacturer Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) rose 4% in Thursday's pre-market trading. This followed a 48% jump in Lenovo's (LNVGY) fiscal second-quarter revenue. The Chinese PC and server rival generated $30.2 billion in sales during the quarter ended September 30. This beat the LSEG consensus estimate of $27.6 billion, boosting sentiment on industry demand.

Lenovo's Q2 2027 Sales Raise Demand Hopes

According to Lenovo, its Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) division posted its best quarter on record. ISG revenue reached $11.3 billion, up 178% from a year ago.

The division handles Lenovo's AI server and storage systems business. It also provides edge computing solutions. This describes products designed to run AI locally on a device for faster response.

In addition, Lenovo's Intelligent Devices Group (IDG) revenue rose 15% year-over-year. The unit reported record second-quarter revenue of $17.4 billion. IDG makes the company's ThinkPad, Yoga, and Legion PCs. It also manufactures tablets, accessories, and Motorola smartphones.

The results show that demand for AI servers remains solid. More importantly, the earnings also show that consumers continue to buy PCs despite price increases. This matters because Lenovo is the world's largest PC maker by unit shipments.

PC makers have been forced to raise prices over the past year as memory chips and other components have become more expensive. Still, Lenovo said it widened its PC market lead over its closest rival, HP (HPQ), by 7.2 percentage points during the quarter.

data.title: Markets Brace for U.S. Jobless Claims and Factory Data After Fed Minutes Lock In Rate Hike Bets
data.description:
A new batch of U.S. economic data hits the tape on Thursday morning, led by weekly jobless claims and factory activity. Investors will be looking for clues on growth less than a day after Federal Reserve minutes cemented bets for higher interest rates next month.

The U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) held near a 19-month high around 103.82 early Thursday, while U.S. stock futures edged higher ahead of the morning releases and AI startup Anthropic's IPO. Meanwhile, spot gold (CM:XAUUSD) hovered near $3,740 an ounce after dropping to a 14-month low of $3,719.10 on Wednesday.

Jobless Claims and Factory Numbers Will Test U.S. Growth

The U.S. Department of Labor releases weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 a.m. ET for the week ended November 14. Economists expect 197,000 new filings, down slightly from the prior week's 200,000 print and just above the four-week average of 195,250. Weekly claims have stayed between 189,000 and 212,000 since mid-July, showing that layoffs remain low across the country.

The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia also publishes its November manufacturing index at 8:30 a.m. ET. Forecasters expect the factory gauge to come in at 20, down slightly from 20.9 in October. Around the same time, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack delivers opening remarks at the central bank's annual Financial Stability Conference.

More reports follow at 10:00 a.m. ET. The Conference Board drops its October Leading Economic Index after the gauge held flat at 99.6 in September. Existing home sales data and third-quarter U.S. Census Bureau reports on e-commerce and services spending also hit the tape at 10:00 a.m. ET.

Federal Reserve Minutes Lock In December Rate Hike Bets

Thursday's reports arrive right after minutes from the Fed's October 27–28 policy meeting reinforced a tough stance on inflation. Officials kept the benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4.00% last month, yet nearly all policymakers backed raising rates again soon to push inflation back to 2%. Two officials even discussed a half-point hike.

"A few participants observed that inflation could prove more persistent than anticipated, in which case a shift to a more restrictive policy stance could become necessary," the Federal Open Market Committee minutes stated.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller added Wednesday that a half-point hike could be needed next month if prices keep climbing. Traders on Thursday priced in a 90% chance of a quarter-point hike and a 10% chance of a half-point increase at the December 8–9 meeting, CME Group's FedWatch tool shows.

Data released earlier this week gave rate hawks plenty of backing. Bureau of Labor Statistics figures showed October import prices jumped 1.1% for a second straight month, topping estimates for a 0.7% rise. Separate Census Bureau numbers showed October retail sales grew 0.2%, while the core control group feeding into GDP rose 0.6%.

High Mortgage Rates Drag Down Home Contracts and Permits

Housing numbers released Wednesday showed high borrowing costs are still squeezing buyers and builders, with 30-year mortgage rates holding above 7.2%. Pending home sales fell 4.7% in October from September and plunged 16.7% from a year ago to their lowest level since 2001, the National Association of Realtors reported.

"October could mark the low point in contract signings for this housing cycle, as mortgage rates appear to have topped out," National Association of Realtors Chief Economist Lawrence Yun said.

Census Bureau construction figures painted a mixed picture for October. Housing starts jumped 9.9% on multi-family projects, though overall building permits slid 7.4%. Single-family permits dropped 8.7% to their slowest pace since May 2020.

In bond markets, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield slipped for a fourth straight session on Thursday to around 5.05%. Safe-haven buying from Middle East tensions and cheaper oil pulled yields slightly lower. West Texas Intermediate crude fell 3.2% Wednesday to $83.26 a barrel after the Energy Information Administration reported a 3.4 million-barrel jump in U.S. crude stockpiles.
data.author: Annika Masrani

data.title: Michael Burry Sounds Alarm on Nvidia's $500B AI Funding Plan: What Went Wrong?
data.description:
The Big Short investor Michael Burry has questioned the progress of a massive $500 billion financing plan tied to Nvidia (NVDA). Despite earlier pledges from some of Wall Street's biggest financial firms, no capital has been deployed so far.

In a post on X on Thursday, Burry shared a report by The Wall Street Journal highlighting delays in the plan, which was first discussed in August. The initiative aims to help Nvidia customers finance AI chip purchases as demand for computing power grows.

Wall Street Giants Have Yet to Put Money to Work

The financing plan involves six major financial firms: Apollo Global Management (APO), Blackstone (BX), BlackRock (BLK), Brookfield Asset Management (BAM), Goldman Sachs (GS), and KKR (KKR).

The firms had agreed to explore ways to raise as much as $500 billion to fund AI chip purchases and related projects. However, their initial commitments were made through a nonbinding memorandum of understanding, meaning they were not legally bound to raise a set amount.

The plan was driven by Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang's efforts to expand funding options for customers building AI data centers. However, talks have faced hurdles over Nvidia's proposed credit guarantees, which could cover up to 25% of project costs.

Lenders are seeking stronger protections before moving ahead. Talks on the first chip-backed financing deal are ongoing, but an agreement is not expected before 2027, according to the report.

Burry Maintains Bearish Bet on NVDA

Burry has maintained his bearish position on Nvidia, holding $140 strike put options expiring in February 2027. Ahead of Nvidia's latest earnings, he ruled out buying short-term call options to hedge against a possible rally, saying, "I am not buying calls, no."

He also noted that retail buying could lift Nvidia shares in the short term, but remains cautious about the longer-term outlook. Beyond his direct Nvidia puts, Burry has bearish exposure through put options on the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the Nasdaq-100 index (NDX).

Burry has also raised concerns about Huang's departure, arguing that Nvidia's grip on the AI supply chain could weaken without its longtime CEO. He believes customers and business partners may have more room to renegotiate deals, delay purchases or turn to competitors, potentially slowing growth and putting pressure on profit margins.

Separately, Burry drew attention to Nvidia's delayed Form 10-Q filing, adding another point of scrutiny around the company.

Is Nvidia a Strong Buy?

On TipRanks, NVDA has a Moderate Buy consensus rating based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell rating. The average Nvidia price target of $232.59 implies 54.1% upside potential from current levels.

data.title: Anthropic IPO: Claude Maker Prepares for Biggest IPO in History at $1.5 Trillion Valuation
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) is set to make history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record. The company behind the Claude AI chatbot priced its shares at $83 each, above its initial range. The IPO values Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. Anthropic is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq (NDAQ) on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT.

The company raised $81.3 billion through the sale of 980 million shares. It is also raising another $26 billion through a private placement, taking the total deal size to $107.3 billion. This puts Anthropic ahead of SpaceX (SPCX), which had set the prior record with its IPO.

Strong Demand Drives Record IPO

The IPO was six times oversubscribed, helping Anthropic price its shares above the top end of its first range. The company had first planned to sell shares at $70 to $78 each, which would have valued it at about $1.4 trillion.

The record IPO comes amid growing concerns about the high cost of AI development and the large sums tech firms are spending on chips and data centers. Anthropic's public debut will give investors a chance to assess the value of a major AI model maker in the public market.

Claude Growth Drives Revenue Higher

Demand for Claude and Claude Code, Anthropic's AI tool for software developers, has helped drive rapid business growth.

Anthropic's third-quarter revenue reached $17 billion, up 47% from the prior quarter and more than 12 times higher than a year earlier. Its annualized revenue run rate (not reported annual revenue) reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30.

The company also reported 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue as of September 30. This compares with more than 1,500 such customers at the end of last year.

High Computing Costs Remain a Key Risk

Despite strong growth, Anthropic faces high costs as it builds and runs its AI systems. The company spent nearly $9 billion on computing and infrastructure in the first half of 2026. It also reported an operating loss of $567 million in the third quarter, compared with operating income of $974 million in the prior quarter.

Anthropic has nearly $900 billion in future computing commitments with partners, including Amazon (AMZN) and Google (GOOGL). These costs will be important to watch as the company expands its AI services.

What Is the Forecast for ANT Stock?

Currently, three research firms have initiated coverage of ANT stock with Buy ratings and bullish price targets. Needham analyst Scott Berg set a $150 target, while New Street Research's five-star analyst Pierre Ferragu set a $105 target. Citizens JMP analyst Patrick Walravens set a $125 target.

Based on the $83 IPO price, these targets point to potential upside of about 81%, 26.5%, and 50.6%, respectively.

data.title: Quantum Computing News: IBM, Nvidia, and AMD Team Up on New Quantum Projects
data.description:
Welcome to Thursday's quantum computing news recap. This edition covers new partnerships involving IBM, Nvidia, and AMD, along with a bigger quantum computing roadmap from Alice & Bob. We also have Infleqtion's latest earnings and a proposed acquisition by SEALSQ that could expand its reach in quantum cybersecurity.

1. Alice & Bob Doubles Its Quantum Computing Target to 200 Logical Qubits

We begin with French quantum computing company Alice & Bob, which unveiled an ambitious new roadmap targeting 200 logical qubits by 2030, double its previous goal. The company plans to reach that milestone using just 3,600 physical cat qubits, which are designed to reduce certain quantum errors directly in the hardware.

The roadmap starts with six logical qubits in 2028, followed by 1,024 in 2032 and 2,048 by 2034. These systems could eventually support applications in materials science, chemistry, and cryptography.

Alice & Bob also plans to connect multiple quantum processors at extremely low temperatures to build larger systems. The company says it has already built and operated three independent processors and demonstrated the key components needed for a logical qubit. The challenge now is turning those early results into working systems at a much larger scale.

2. SEALSQ Plans Acquisition of Quantum Cybersecurity Firm QuintessenceLabs

SEALSQ Corp. (LAES) has signed a non-binding letter of intent to acquire 100% of Australian quantum cybersecurity company QuintessenceLabs. The proposed purchase would be funded through a mix of cash and SEALSQ shares, although the companies have not disclosed a deal value.

The acquisition would combine SEALSQ's secure chips and post-quantum security products with QuintessenceLabs' quantum random number generation, encryption key management, and secure communications technologies. The goal is to offer broader security solutions to governments, banks, and businesses preparing for future quantum computing threats.

The companies have entered a 60-day exclusivity period and are targeting completion in the first half of 2027. The deal is not final, and the new shares issued to fund it would dilute existing SEALSQ shareholders.

3. IBM and Nvidia Join Fermilab to Develop Quantum Supercomputing

IBM (IBM), Nvidia (NVDA), and Fermilab announced a collaboration to develop a modular quantum computing platform for scientific research.

The project will combine IBM's quantum processors, Nvidia's accelerated computing technology, and Fermilab's expertise in superconducting hardware. Researchers plan to focus on complex problems in particle physics, nuclear science, and neutrino research.

One goal is to connect quantum computers with conventional supercomputing systems, allowing researchers to use both technologies in the same workflow. Fermilab also plans to contribute superconducting cavity technology that could help store quantum information and reduce errors.

The collaboration remains a research effort rather than a commercial product launch, but it could help researchers design quantum systems around real scientific problems.

4. Infleqtion Revenue Climbs 57% as Quantum Technology Advances

Quantum computing company Infleqtion (INFQ) reported $32.6 million in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, up 57% from a year earlier. Third-quarter revenue reached $9.1 million, a 25% increase.

The growth came alongside rising costs. Infleqtion's third-quarter operating loss widened to $34.5 million from $6.7 million a year ago, showing how expensive developing quantum technology remains.

On the technology side, Infleqtion demonstrated 30 entangled logical qubits using 80 physical qubits on its Sqale system. The company says AI helped cut the number of physical gates needed for a key operation by half.

Infleqtion is now targeting 100 logical qubits by 2028. It also secured a $20 million NASA contract expansion for quantum gravity sensing technology, adding to its growing work with government customers.

5. AMD and IQM Demonstrate Hybrid Quantum Computing for Chemistry

We end with Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and IQM Quantum Computers (IQMX), which demonstrated a hybrid computing system that combines quantum processors with conventional GPUs to solve chemistry problems.

The project used IQM's 20-qubit Garnet processor alongside AMD Instinct GPUs to calculate the energy of hydrogen molecules. Researchers tested the system across 17 different molecular bond lengths, showing that the two computing technologies could work together.

The partners also released the workflow as an open-source Jupyter notebook, allowing developers to explore the approach. The test did not demonstrate that quantum computers outperform classical systems. Instead, it showed that quantum hardware and AMD's GPU software can work together in a complete computing process.

The companies now plan to explore more complex molecules and tighter connections between the two systems, with the goal of making hybrid quantum computing more useful for scientific research.

data.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 19: Anthropic's $81 Billion IPO Takes Center Stage
data.description:
U.S. stock futures moved higher ahead of Thursday's opening bell as investors focused on Anthropic's (ANT) highly anticipated Nasdaq debut. The maker of Claude AI is targeting a potential $1.5 trillion valuation, making it one of the largest IPOs in history.

Futures on the Nasdaq-100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were up 2.07%, 1.16%, and 0.57%, respectively, as of 5:40 a.m. EST on November 19.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its initial target range of $70 to $78, following strong investor demand. The company also increased the offering size from 825 million to 980 million shares. The IPO is expected to raise approximately $81.34 billion, surpassing SpaceX's (SPCX) $75 billion June offering to become the largest IPO on record. The company is also raising an additional $26 billion through a private placement.

Meanwhile, oil prices edged higher on Thursday after falling in the previous session. Concerns about rising global oil supply and higher U.S. interest rates limited gains, while renewed geopolitical risks in the Middle East supported prices. Reports of possible further U.S. action against Iran and attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz also kept supply concerns in focus.

At the time of writing, Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, rose 0.76% to $92.65 per barrel, while WTI crude futures rose 0.65% to $83.80 per barrel.

During Wednesday's regular trading session, the three major U.S. indexes closed mixed. The DJIA fell 1.11%, while the S&P 500 declined 0.23%, marking its fifth straight day of losses. The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.42%.

Looking ahead, investors will also watch data on weekly jobless claims for further clues about the strength of the U.S. labor market. On the earnings front, results from Walmart (WMT), Alibaba (BABA), and Gap (GAP) are scheduled for release today. 

Global Markets

European markets traded mixed on Thursday, while Asia-Pacific markets closed mostly lower. Investors remained cautious ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, as concerns about AI valuations and the outlook for U.S. interest rates continued to weigh on sentiment.

Investors also kept an eye on the trilateral meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The talks could focus on nuclear arms control, the Ukraine war, and global security. Any progress could ease geopolitical tensions and improve investor sentiment.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index dropped 1.95%. In China, the Shanghai Composite fell 0.28%, and the Shenzhen Component was down 1.20%. The Nikkei 225 added 0.71% and the Topix declined 0.04%.

data.title: Morgan Stanley Says AI Has a Labor Problem — and These 2 'Strong Buy' Stocks Could Cash In
data.description:
Despite recent setbacks, including the scandal surrounding Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang, growing concerns over excessive AI spending, and political uncertainty following the midterm elections, AI remains a key growth driver. However, the opportunities extend beyond chip giants, cloud computing providers, and software developers, with companies responsible for building the infrastructure needed to support AI also positioned to benefit.

Morgan Stanley analyst Stephan Diaz sees considerable potential in the Engineering and Construction (E&C) sector, where demand for skilled workers is outpacing supply. As AI infrastructure projects become larger and more complex, companies with established workforces and specialized expertise could gain a competitive advantage. Diaz believes this labor shortage could translate into stronger growth for leading E&C companies.

"Large Engineering and Construction (E&C) companies have established positions in one of the infrastructure buildout's key bottlenecks: skilled labor. The training and experience required to develop crews make that capacity difficult to replicate quickly. Most operate in highly specialized verticals such as high and low voltage electric, HVAC, plumbing, and civil. To help safeguard the skilled labor advantage companies in our coverage own, operate, and implement schools, training programs, and staffing companies. Alongside national footprints and strong balance sheets, this supports outsized growth in a narrowly growing non-residential construction market driven by share gains as projects continue to skew larger, more remote, and more complex," Diaz explained.

With this opportunity in mind, Diaz has highlighted two E&C stocks that could benefit from the growing demand for AI infrastructure. Using the TipRanks database, we've taken a closer look at two of his picks, both of which carry Strong Buy consensus ratings from Wall Street. Here's what makes these companies worth watching.

Comfort Systems USA (FIX)

The first stock we'll look at, Comfort Systems USA, is a mechanical and electrical contract service provider, based in Houston, Texas. The company is a member of the S&P 500 index and has been since December of last year. Comfort Systems is a holding company with a network of 50-plus operating companies that provide services across 184 locations in the US. The engineering services provided include building and support for mechanical, electrical, modular, and plumbing building systems – the systems necessary to put empty building shells into operation.

Comfort Systems operates through two segments: Mechanical, which covers HVAC, plumbing, process piping, modular and off-site construction, fire protection, and building automation; and Electrical, which includes installation, servicing, and system integration. Its services also span the building lifecycle, including new construction, ongoing maintenance, retrofits, and renovations.

The stock has been volatile this year due to swinging sentiment in the AI sector – it peaked above $2,000 in the summer, and is down 41% in the past six months – but even with that, FIX shares are still up some 18% for the year-to-date.

Looking at the company's most recent set of financials, we find that Comfort Systems reported $3.77 billion in revenue for 3Q26, up more than 53% year-over-year and more than $365 million better than had been expected. The diluted EPS of $13.91 beat the forecast by $1.06. The company's outlook is also supported by its growing order backlog, which reached $17.81 billion at the end of Q3, up almost 90% year-over-year.

Morgan Stanley's Diaz starts with that backlog in his discussion of Comfort Systems and from there he looks at the stock's prospects in the coming year, writing, "Current backlog levels suggest growth above and beyond our own forecasts when assuming historical conversion rates hold, suggesting opportunity for positive earnings revisions. In addition, strong hyperscaler capex growth, where MS is ahead of street estimates, and a differentiated modular business where FIX has guided to 50% capacity growth in 2027 supports this sentiment. Moreover, the recent de-rating in shares has made for an attractive entry point for a company that recently posted accelerating bookings, guided 2027 to mid-twenties revenue growth, and has the ability to expand its modular offering beyond guided levels due to its net cash position and given current capacity investment plans are with current customers only (mainly 2 hyperscalers)."

Quantifying this stance, Diaz puts an Overweight (i.e., Buy) rating on the stock, along with a $1,410 price target that implies a one-year upside potential of ~24%. (To watch Diaz's track record, click here)

Wall Street is even more bullish, with the average price target of $1,849 suggesting shares could surge 62% from current levels. All eight recent analyst ratings are Buys, giving FIX stock a unanimous Strong Buy consensus rating. (See FIX stock forecast)

EMCOR Group (EME)

EMCOR, the next stock we'll look at, is another multi-billion-dollar player in the US construction industry. The company traces its business roots back to 1966, but has been operating in its current incarnation since 1994. EMCOR offers construction services, building services, and industrial services – three core divisions that together make up a vital chunk of the Construction and Engineering segment.

Through its construction services, EMCOR builds and maintains power systems, data centers, and semiconductor plants, and provides them with HVAC installations, fire protection, and modern industrial piping. The building services segment overlaps with HVAC and plumbing, and also includes energy solutions and facility management. Finally, industrial services include work involving refineries, carbon capture, water treatment, and other vital infrastructure. EMCOR works with customers in both the commercial and government sectors.

EMCOR works through a network of about 100 subsidiary operating companies. This network has well over 400 locations across the US, and generated $16.99 billion in revenues last year. And, to build out the array of services it provides, EMCOR has over 47,000 skilled-labor employees, bringing skill and expertise to the ambitious construction projects.

Earlier this month, EMCOR revealed that it has entered an agreement to acquire P1 Construction, a mechanical and electrical contractor serving high-growth markets in the Midwest. The deal was announced as an all-cash transaction, but exact terms were not released.

The last quarterly report covered 3Q26, and showed strong gains from 3Q25. Revenue was up almost 29% year-over-year, and hit $5.54 billion. Earnings were up 46.1%; the non-GAAP EPS of $9.60 beat the forecast by $1.24 per share. And, like Comfort Systems above, EMCOR has a strong work backlog – it reported remaining performance obligations of $18.57 billion at the end of Q3, for a 47.2% year-over-year jump.

All of this explains why analyst Diaz is bullish here. In his coverage for Morgan Stanley, he states, "With a history of solid execution, current backlog levels suggest upside to consensus estimates in 2027, and an undemanding valuation, we view the set-up favorable for EME. Data center work is also a growing share of that backlog, which in the current macro environment will likely be met with question marks. That said, EME's data center exposure is ~70%/30% cloud vs. AI which should help sentiment. In addition, we find EME's M&A strategy particularly attractive as the company has shown it can pay below public company multiples for contractors without material data center exposure and then layer its own data center pipeline on top, effectively acquiring skilled craft labor, the industry's main bottleneck, at a discount to its own multiple. We view EME as a lower beta way to gain exposure to the AI infrastructure demand cycle given its exposure to union labor, more diversified end markets and lower fixed investment risk to data centers vs. FIX."

Reflecting his confidence, Diaz rates EME as Overweight (i.e., Buy), with a $799 price target suggesting shares could climb ~24% over the next 12 months.

The rest of the Street shares that positive outlook, with 6 Buys and 2 Holds giving EME a Strong Buy consensus rating. At its current price of $644.17, the stock offers a 31.5% potential upside, based on the average analyst target of $849.71. (See EME stock forecast)

data.title: Neocloud Stocks Are Rising in Pre-Market After Anthropic's Record $81.3B IPO Raise — Here's Why
data.description:
Shares in neocloud companies CoreWeave (CRWV), Nebius (NBIS), and IREN (IREN) are rising in Thursday's pre-market session. This came after Claude chatbot creator Anthropic (ANT) on Wednesday priced its initial public offering (IPO) on Nasdaq at $83 per share, raising $81.3 billion. The IPO raise surpassed the record $75 billion rocket giant SpaceX (SPCX) raised in its July market debut.

The IPO matters for AI cloud firms as it gives Anthropic extra capital for its AI buildout. Of note, Anthropic is already a CoreWeave customer. IREN is also believed to have secured a multi-year AI cloud deal with the AI developer.

Anthropic Attracts Strong Demand for Its IPO

Anthropic initially aimed to sell its shares at $70 to $78 per share. However, strong investor demand pushed the figure to $83 per share.

The Amazon (AMZN)-backed company also sold more shares: 980 million, compared to its earlier target of 825 million. The IPO is expected to raise Anthropic's valuation to $1.5 trillion.

The company's shares will start trading at market open today under the ticker symbol "ANT."
